interpretations.scope_boundary: In scope: a new tools/preflight-export.sh that bundles a single consumer's accumulated .preflight/ state (decisions/*.jsonl, gate/ evidence, cache/derived-state.json) plus the installed.lock manifest into one portable, self-describing archive. Boundary: it only reads and packages existing on-disk state — it does not interpret, transform, redact, or re-import that data, and it touches nothing outside the consumer's .preflight/ tree.
surfaces_in_scope: tools/preflight-export.sh (new, modeled on preflight-verify.sh/preflight-install.sh: takes <CONSUMER_DIR>, exit-code disciplined)
.preflight/gate/ and .preflight/cache/derived-state.json (gate evidence + derived state included in the bundle)
installed.lock manifest (read to stamp framework version/provenance into the export)
tests/behavioral/ (a new behavioral test proving the export produces a complete, well-formed archive)
surfaces_out_of_scope: Any notion of SaaS accounts, user profiles, or a database of 'users' — none exists in this repo
An import/restore path (export is one-directional; round-trip is a separate item)
Redaction, anonymization, or filtering of decision-log contents
GDPR/DSAR-style legal-export semantics or PII handling
Modifying the installer, hooks, or gate-clearance logic
A web UI or any interactive download surface
interpretations.core_behavior: Running tools/preflight-export.sh against a consumer dir reads that repo's accumulated .preflight/ state and writes it to a single self-describing, provenance-stamped archive the user can carry off, with a disciplined exit code on success/failure.

interpretations.scope_boundary: In scope: a new read-only `tools/preflight-export.sh` that bundles one consumer repo's local preflight runtime/learning data (everything under `.preflight/`: metrics.json, captures, decisions, adjudications, gate evidence, config, plus the resolved rubric) into a single portable, timestamped archive with a manifest. The boundary stops at reading-and-packaging existing on-disk state — no new data is collected, nothing is mutated/deleted, no import/restore side, no end-user/account product (none exists in this repo), no network/upload, and no change to how preflight writes data.
surfaces_in_scope: tools/preflight-export.sh (new export utility, sibling to preflight-verify.sh / preflight-install.sh)
Consumer .preflight/ tree as the read source: metrics.json, capture files (calibration-log/checklist-additions/false-positives/pattern-capture), decisions/, adjudications/, gate/, config.json
The resolved rubric path(s) (via lib/resolve-config.sh / rubric-resolve.sh) so exported captures stay interpretable
An export manifest (surface list + source HEAD + tag + timestamp) written into the archive, mirroring the installer's installed.lock manifest discipline
tests/behavioral/ — a behavioral test proving the archive is produced and round-trips the expected files (CLAUDE.md certification rule)
surfaces_out_of_scope: Any end-user-facing product, web UI, account system, or customer database (this repo has none — not GDPR/customer data export)
An import/restore command — export only this pass
Modifying how skills/hooks write .preflight data, or adding new telemetry fields
Uploading/syncing the archive anywhere (no network, no CI aggregation — explicitly future work per metrics.md)
Deleting or redacting source data, or any mutation of the consumer repo
Exporting service/source code or git history — only preflight operational state
Installer/verifier/hooks changes beyond reusing their config-resolution helpers
interpretations.core_behavior: Add `tools/preflight-export.sh <CONSUMER_DIR>` that reads (never mutates) the consumer's `.preflight/` runtime state plus the resolved rubric and writes a single timestamped, manifest-bearing archive the team can carry to another machine or attach to a report.

interpretations.scope_boundary: In scope: a new `tools/preflight-export.sh` that bundles a single consumer repo's `.preflight/` working-state directory into one portable archive (tarball) the operator can hand off or relocate. Boundary: export only — read the existing state, write an archive; no import/restore, no schema transform, no filtering of secrets beyond what is already gitignored, and nothing touching the framework SOURCE surfaces.
surfaces_in_scope: tools/preflight-export.sh (new operator command — the export entrypoint)
the consumer-side .preflight/ tree as the data source (config.json, gate/, adjudications/, decisions/, metrics.json, track-record/, installed.lock, derived/)
a behavioral test under tests/behavioral/ wired into tests/run-all-tests.sh proving the archive is produced and contains the expected state files
surfaces_out_of_scope: no import/restore command (export is one-directional)
no changes to preflight-install.sh / preflight-verify.sh or the manifest/installed.lock format
no hooks/ gate changes and no new PreToolUse enforcement
no export of framework SOURCE surfaces (agents/ skills/ lib/ hooks/ — those are installed artifacts, not operator data)
no redaction/secret-scrubbing engine and no cloud upload/transport
no config-schema migration or format conversion of the exported state
interpretations.core_behavior: Running `preflight-export.sh <CONSUMER_DIR>` reads that consumer's `.preflight/` working-state tree and writes it to a single timestamped archive (e.g. `preflight-export-<ts>.tar.gz`), failing closed if the directory is absent or unreadable.

interpretations.scope_boundary: Add one new read-only CLI tool, tools/preflight-export.sh, that bundles a consumer's own accumulated .preflight/ run-state (decisions log, adjudications, gate evidence, cache, metrics, track-record, migration checkpoint, config) into a single portable, self-describing archive (a manifest + tar/zip) written outside the repo working tree; it reads existing files and writes nothing back into .preflight/. Scope ends at producing the archive — no re-import, no upload, no transport, no UI.
surfaces_in_scope: tools/preflight-export.sh (the new tool — gathers tracked + ignored .preflight/ artifacts and emits an archive + a JSON manifest stamping source repo, HEAD SHA, framework tag, and timestamp)

tests/behavioral/ (a new export-test.sh proving the archive is produced, contains the expected artifacts, and the tool exits non-zero with no archive when .preflight/ is absent — wired into tests/run-all-tests.sh)
Commands section of CLAUDE.md and the tools overview in FRAMEWORK.md (document the new tool alongside preflight-install/verify so the single-source docs do not diverge)
surfaces_out_of_scope: Any import/restore path that reads an archive back into a repo (export only, one direction)
Uploading, emailing, or transporting the archive anywhere (it lands on local disk; the user moves it)
Hooks/gates — export is read-only and does not create or clear any .preflight/gate/ evidence, so no PreToolUse gate is added
Web/product-style data-export endpoints, user accounts, or a GUI — there is no service or DB in this repo; 'their data' is the framework's per-run .preflight/ state, not application data
Changing what is gitignored vs tracked, or altering the install/prune manifest contract
Redaction/anonymization or encryption of the exported contents (out of scope for this first cut)
interpretations.core_behavior: Running tools/preflight-export.sh <CONSUMER_DIR> collects that consumer's .preflight/ run-state into one timestamped, manifest-stamped archive on local disk that the user can take elsewhere, reading existing files only and never mutating the repo.
